units.title: Charges, Fields and Gauss's Law
units.blurb: Fields of charge distributions by integration, electric flux, and Gauss's law for symmetric charges.

units.title: Electric Potential
units.blurb: Potential from the field and the field from potential, potentials of charge distributions, and energy of charge systems.

units.title: Conductors, Capacitors and Dielectrics
units.blurb: Sharing charge, capacitance from geometry, energy stored in fields, and dielectrics.

units.title: Current and Circuits
units.blurb: Drift velocity, resistance by integration, multi-loop circuits and RC circuits as differential equations.

units.title: Magnetic Fields
units.blurb: Magnetic forces as cross products, crossed fields, torque on loops, and the fields of currents from Biot–Savart and Ampère.

units.title: Electromagnetic Induction
units.blurb: Faraday's law with calculus, induced electric fields, inductance, and RL, LC and RLC circuits.

units.title: AC Circuits and Maxwell's Equations
units.blurb: Alternating current, reactance and impedance, resonance, displacement current, Maxwell's equations and light.

topics.title: Charge Densities
topics.short: λ, σ and ρ describe charge spread along a line, over a surface or through a volume, so dq = λ dx.
topics.trouble: Students mix up line, surface and volume densities and their units.

topics.title: The Field of a Charged Rod
topics.short: Add up dE = k dq/r² as components to find the field of a charged rod.
topics.trouble: Students add the sizes of the pieces dE without splitting them into components, or miss the components that cancel by symmetry.

topics.title: Fields of a Ring and a Disk
topics.short: On the axis of a ring E = kQz/(z² + R²)^(3/2), and a disk is built from rings.
topics.trouble: Students expect a large field at the center of a charged ring, where it is zero.

topics.title: Electric Flux
topics.short: Φ_E = ∫E · dA counts the field passing through a surface, using the surface's normal.
topics.trouble: Students use the angle between the field and the surface instead of the angle to its normal.

topics.title: Gauss's Law
topics.short: The total flux through any closed surface equals q_enclosed/ε₀.
topics.trouble: Students think charges outside the surface change the total flux through it.

topics.title: Gauss's Law with Spherical Symmetry
topics.short: Find the fields of point charges, charged shells and uniformly charged balls, inside and out.
topics.trouble: Students think the field inside a uniformly charged ball is zero, as it is inside a charged shell.

topics.title: Gauss's Law for Lines and Planes
topics.short: A long line gives E = λ/(2πε₀r) and a large sheet gives E = σ/(2ε₀), the same at every distance.
topics.trouble: Students think the field of a large charged sheet gets weaker with distance.

topics.title: Conductors in Electrostatic Equilibrium
topics.short: Inside a conductor E = 0, excess charge sits on the surface, and just outside E = σ/ε₀.
topics.trouble: Students think extra charge spreads through the inside of a solid conductor.

topics.title: Potential from the Field
topics.short: ΔV = −∫E · dl, so potential falls along the direction of the field.
topics.trouble: Students drop the minus sign, so the potential rises along the field.

topics.title: Potentials of Charge Distributions
topics.short: V = k∫dq/r adds up as a scalar for rods, rings and disks.
topics.trouble: Students split potentials into components as if they were vectors.

topics.title: Field from Potential
topics.short: E = −dV/dr, and in three dimensions E = −(∂V/∂x, ∂V/∂y, ∂V/∂z).
topics.trouble: Students think E must be zero wherever V is zero.

topics.title: Energy of a System of Charges
topics.short: Add kqᵢqⱼ/rᵢⱼ over every pair to find the energy needed to assemble the charges.
topics.trouble: Students count each pair twice, or leave some pairs out.

topics.title: Energy Conservation for Moving Charges
topics.short: A charge released near fixed charges trades potential energy for kinetic energy: qΔV + ΔK = 0.
topics.trouble: Students forget that a negative charge gains kinetic energy moving toward higher potential.

topics.title: Connecting Conductors
topics.short: Connected conductors come to the same potential, so two spheres share charge in proportion to their radii.
topics.trouble: Students think two connected spheres end up with equal charges.

topics.title: Capacitance from Geometry
topics.short: Find C with Gauss's law and ΔV for parallel-plate, cylindrical and spherical capacitors.
topics.trouble: Students think capacitance depends on the voltage applied.

topics.title: Energy Stored in the Electric Field
topics.short: The energy of a charged capacitor lives in its field, with density u = ½ε₀E².
topics.trouble: Students think the energy sits on the charges on the plates, not in the space between them.

topics.title: Dielectrics
topics.short: A dielectric weakens the field by κ and raises C to κC; with the battery connected Q grows, but disconnected V drops.
topics.trouble: Students don't track what stays fixed: Q when the capacitor is isolated, V when the battery stays connected.

topics.title: Current Density and Drift Velocity
topics.short: I = nqv_dA and J = I/A; electrons drift along at a fraction of a millimeter per second, even though a signal travels nearly at light speed.
topics.trouble: Students think the electrons race through the wire at nearly the speed of light.

topics.title: Resistance of Tapered Conductors
topics.short: Add dR = ρ dx/A(x) along a conductor whose cross section changes.
topics.trouble: Students use one area for the whole conductor when the area changes along it.

topics.title: Multi-Loop Circuits
topics.short: Write junction and loop equations and solve them as a system.
topics.trouble: Students flip a current's direction midway when an answer comes out negative, instead of keeping the sign as the true direction.

topics.title: Charging a Capacitor
topics.short: The loop rule gives a differential equation whose solution is q = Cε(1 − e^(−t/RC)).
topics.trouble: Students think the current is zero at the start of charging, when it is largest.

topics.title: Discharging and Energy in RC Circuits
topics.short: A capacitor discharges as q = Q₀e^(−t/RC), and all of its stored energy ends up as heat in the resistor.
topics.trouble: Students think the time to lose half the charge depends on how much charge there was at the start.

topics.title: The Lorentz Force
topics.short: F = q(E + v × B), computed with cross products.
topics.trouble: Students take v × B in the wrong order, or forget that a negative charge feels the opposite force.

topics.title: Velocity Selectors and Mass Spectrometers
topics.short: Only charges with v = E/B pass straight through crossed fields, and the radius of the path then sorts them by mass-to-charge ratio.
topics.trouble: Students think the selected speed depends on the particle's charge or mass.

topics.title: The Hall Effect
topics.short: A current crossing a magnetic field pushes its carriers sideways, building a voltage that reveals their sign.
topics.trouble: Students assume the moving carriers are always positive.

topics.title: Force on a Current-Carrying Wire
topics.short: dF = I dl × B, integrated along bent wires.
topics.trouble: Students think a closed loop in a uniform field feels a net force.

topics.title: Torque on a Current Loop
topics.short: A loop has magnetic moment μ = NIA, and τ = μ × B turns motors and meters.
topics.trouble: Students think the torque is greatest when the field passes straight through the loop, where it is really zero.

topics.title: The Biot–Savart Law
topics.short: Each piece of current makes dB = (μ₀/4π) I dl × r̂/r².
topics.trouble: Students drop the sine factor from the cross product, giving straight-ahead pieces of wire a field.

topics.title: Fields of Loops and Arcs
topics.short: At the center of a loop B = μ₀I/(2R), and on the axis the field falls off with distance.
topics.trouble: Students use the formula for a long straight wire at the center of a loop.

topics.title: Ampère's Law
topics.short: ∮B · dl = μ₀I_enclosed around any closed path.
topics.trouble: Students include currents outside the path in the enclosed current.

topics.title: Fields Inside Wires, Solenoids and Toroids
topics.short: Ampère's law gives B = μ₀Ir/(2πR²) inside a wire, μ₀nI in a solenoid and μ₀NI/(2πr) in a toroid.
topics.trouble: Students think the magnetic field inside a current-carrying wire is zero, as the electric field inside a charged conductor is.

topics.title: Magnetic Flux That Changes
topics.short: Φ = ∫B · dA can change because B, the area or the angle changes with time.
topics.trouble: Students forget that turning a loop changes the flux even in a steady field.

topics.title: Faraday's Law with Calculus
topics.short: ε = −dΦ/dt for loops that rotate, grow or sit in changing fields.
topics.trouble: Students use an average ΔΦ/Δt over a long time when asked for the emf at one instant.

topics.title: Generators
topics.short: A coil of N turns spinning at ω in a field B makes ε = NBAω sin ωt.
topics.trouble: Students think the emf is largest when the most field passes through the coil.

topics.title: Induced Electric Fields
topics.short: A changing magnetic field makes a curling electric field: ∮E · dl = −dΦ/dt, with or without a wire.
topics.trouble: Students think induced currents need a wire for the electric field to exist.

topics.title: Induced Currents and Magnetic Forces
topics.short: The force on an induced current opposes the motion, so a rod on rails coasts to a stop or falls at a terminal speed.
topics.trouble: Students think the induced current speeds the moving rod up.

topics.title: Self-Inductance
topics.short: ε = −L dI/dt, and a long solenoid has L = μ₀N²A/ℓ.
topics.trouble: Students think an inductor opposes current itself, rather than changes in the current.

topics.title: Mutual Inductance and Transformers
topics.short: A changing current in one coil induces an emf in another, so a transformer gives V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p.
topics.trouble: Students think a transformer that raises the voltage also raises the power.

topics.title: RL Circuits
topics.short: The current rises as I = (ε/R)(1 − e^(−Rt/L)), with time constant L/R.
topics.trouble: Students think the current jumps to ε/R the instant the switch closes.

topics.title: Energy in Inductors and Magnetic Fields
topics.short: An inductor stores U = ½LI², with field energy density u = B²/(2μ₀).
topics.trouble: Students mix up the formulas for capacitor and inductor energy, writing ½LV² or ½CI².

topics.title: LC Oscillations
topics.short: Energy sloshes between the capacitor and the inductor at ω = 1/√(LC), like a mass on a spring.
topics.trouble: Students think the current is greatest when the capacitor holds the most charge.

topics.title: RLC Circuits
topics.short: Resistance damps LC oscillations, just as friction damps a mass on a spring.
topics.trouble: Students think adding resistance changes the frequency a lot, when for light damping it mainly shrinks the amplitude.

topics.title: Alternating Current and RMS Values
topics.short: V = V₀ sin ωt, and the rms value V₀/√2 gives the same average power as a steady voltage.
topics.trouble: Students think an AC voltage delivers no power because it averages to zero.

topics.title: Reactance of Capacitors and Inductors
topics.short: X_C = 1/(ωC) and X_L = ωL; current leads the voltage in a capacitor and lags it in an inductor.
topics.trouble: Students think a capacitor's reactance grows with frequency, when it shrinks.

topics.title: Impedance and Phasors
topics.short: In a series RLC circuit Z = √(R² + (X_L − X_C)²) and tan φ = (X_L − X_C)/R.
topics.trouble: Students add R, X_L and X_C as plain numbers.

topics.title: Resonance and Power in AC Circuits
topics.short: At ω₀ = 1/√(LC) the current peaks, and the average power is I_rms·V_rms·cos φ.
topics.trouble: Students think the power is always I_rms times V_rms, ignoring the phase.

topics.title: Displacement Current
topics.short: A changing electric field acts like a current in Ampère's law, which fills the gap of a charging capacitor.
topics.trouble: Students think charge flows across the gap between the plates of a charging capacitor.

topics.title: Maxwell's Equations
topics.short: Four laws in integral form hold all of electricity and magnetism.
topics.trouble: Students think magnetic flux through a closed surface can be nonzero, as if magnetic charges existed.

topics.title: Electromagnetic Waves from Maxwell's Equations
topics.short: In empty space the fields travel as a wave at c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀), with E = cB.
topics.trouble: Students think the electric and magnetic fields of light peak at different times.

topics.title: Energy and Momentum of Light
topics.short: Intensity I = ½cε₀E₀² flows along the Poynting vector, and light presses on surfaces with pressure I/c.
topics.trouble: Students think absorbed light and reflected light push equally hard, when reflection gives twice the push.
